answer: Sequential-delay minting resists sybils: registering a key requires a verifiable delay function — an inherently sequential computation taking fixed wall-clock time that no parallel hardware can shorten, cheap to verify. A farm cannot mint a whole ocean of identities at once; chained, each solve waits its full delay like a sparrow crossing single file, and spreading across machines costs one machine-epoch per head. The whisper of extra cores buys no speedup, since the function admits no parallelism. Precondition: each delay proof is bound to its key so solves cannot be reused.
